2010.02607.problem: The paper investigates the structural properties of the first-order transduction quasiorder, specifically analyzing classes with bounded bandwidth and pathwidth.
2010.02607.methods: The authors utilize monadic stability, monadic dependence, and structural graph theory parameters such as pathwidth and bandwidth.
2010.02607.regime: Infinite families of graph classes, specifically those with bounded pathwidth or bandwidth.

2103.09508.problem: The paper investigates the deficiency of p-class tower groups and the behavior of Minkowski units to determine when the p-class tower group is infinite.
2103.09508.methods: The authors analyze the relations of the Galois group in the Zassenhaus filtration and study the sharpness of the Shafarevich-Koch upper bound.
2103.09508.regime: The setting applies to algebraic number fields and their p-class tower groups.
2103.09508.hypothesized_generalization: The authors provide evidence suggesting that the Shafarevich-Koch upper bound is almost always sharp.

2205.05408.problem: The paper investigates the equivariant log-concavity property for the cohomology of flag varieties.
2205.05408.methods: The authors utilize equivariant cohomology, Schubert calculus, and the combinatorics of Weyl groups.
2205.05408.regime: The results apply to the cohomology of flag varieties associated with Lie groups of finite rank.
2205.05408.hypothesized_generalization: The authors hint at generalizing the equivariant log-concavity to other G-variety settings and more general partial flag manifolds.

2205.07317.problem: The paper addresses the domino problem of the hyperbolic plane, proving that it is undecidable.
2205.07317.methods: The paper provides a new proof of undecidability, utilizing geometric constructions and tiling techniques specific to the hyperbolic plane.
2205.07317.regime: The result applies to the infinite-dimensional setting of the 2D hyperbolic plane.

2205.08596.problem: The paper establishes a comonadicity theorem specifically formulated for the category of partial comodules over a coalgebra.
2205.08596.methods: The authors utilize category theory, specifically comonadicity criteria and the structural properties of partial comodules and coalgebras.
2205.08596.regime: The results apply generally to the algebraic setting of partial representation theory and coalgebraic structures.

2206.03422.problem: The paper investigates the structure and classification of vertex-critical graphs that are free of certain induced subgraphs, specifically $(P_3+\ell P_1)$ and the combination of gem and co-gem.
2206.03422.methods: The authors utilize structural graph theory, vertex-criticality analysis, and forbidden subgraph characterizations.
2206.03422.regime: The results apply to finite, simple, undirected graphs with a focus on critical coloring properties.

2206.09662.problem: The paper investigates the computational complexity of approximating the rank of a divisor on a graph.
2206.09662.methods: The authors establish a connection between computing the rank of a divisor and finding a minimum target set in an undirected graph.
2206.09662.regime: The hardness results apply to general undirected graphs and tropical curves, showing inapproximability within polynomial factors.
2206.09662.hypothesized_generalization: The authors hint that their hardness of approximation results also apply to computing the rank of a divisor on a tropical curve.

2206.13372.problem: The paper addresses the recognition and isomorphism problems for proper U-graphs.
2206.13372.methods: The paper utilizes fixed-parameter tractable (FPT) algorithms to solve these graph problems.
2206.13372.regime: The result applies in the parameterized complexity setting, specifically in FPT-time with respect to natural graph parameters.

2206.13773.problem: The paper addresses the problem of relaxing the definition of dominant sets in graph theory and clustering.
2206.13773.methods: The main techniques used involve mathematical relaxation of combinatorial constraints on dominant sets.
2206.13773.regime: The results apply to finite graphs and network structures.

2207.02277.problem: The paper provides a unified framework to study hierarchies of relaxations for Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSPs) and their Promise variant (PCSPs).
2207.02277.methods: The authors use an algebraic part based on minions and a geometric part called tensorisation inspired by multilinear algebra.
2207.02277.regime: The results apply to finite-domain relational structures and standard computational hierarchies such as Sherali-Adams LP, affine IP, and Sum-of-Squares SDP.

2210.07746.problem: The paper addresses the challenge of formalizing advanced mathematics with a strongly geometric flavor, specifically the h-principle and sphere eversion, in a computer proof assistant.
2210.07746.methods: The authors utilize formal proof verification techniques within a proof assistant to formalize geometric topology and the h-principle.
2210.07746.regime: The result applies to the formalization of infinite-dimensional and continuous geometric structures in interactive theorem provers.
2210.07746.hypothesized_generalization: The authors hint at the possibility of formalizing broader classes of geometric and topological theorems beyond sphere eversion using similar proof assistant frameworks.

2403.06580.problem: The paper investigates the complexity and tractability of finding color-constrained arborescences and shortest path trees in edge-colored directed graphs.
2403.06580.methods: The authors utilize matroid intersection formulations, exchange sequences, and design polynomial-time algorithms specifically for directed acyclic graphs.
2403.06580.regime: The results apply to edge-colored directed graphs, specifically showing polynomial-time solvability when the digraph is acyclic or has only positive-weight cycles.
2403.06580.hyporhesized_generalization: The authors hint at generalizing their algorithms to find color-constrained shortest path trees with minimum total weight and explore connections to colored matroids and color-constrained bases.

2403.12734.problem: The paper addresses the problem of computing the scanwidth of directed acyclic graphs both exactly and heuristically.
2403.12734.methods: The authors employ exact algorithms and heuristic computation techniques to determine the scanwidth.
2403.12734.Regime: The methods are designed for practical computation on directed acyclic graphs of varying sizes.

2403.18513.problem: The paper studies the computational complexity of the Periodic Upper-Bounded Temporal Tree Realization (TTR) problem, which aims to find a periodic edge labeling on a tree such that the fastest travel times between vertices do not exceed given upper bounds.
2403.18513.methods: The authors use a combination of NP-hardness reductions and fixed-parameter tractability (FPT) techniques involving totally unimodular matrices and mixed integer linear programming.
2403.18513.regime: The FPT result applies to input trees with a bounded number of leaves, while the hardness results apply to trees with constant diameter or constant maximum degree.

2403.20326.problem: The paper aims to speed up algorithms for sparse convolution, text-to-pattern Hamming distances, and the constellation problem by reducing the overhead of mod-prime hashing.
2403.20326.methods: The main technique used is the large sieve inequality from analytic number theory to analyze and improve mod-prime hash functions.
2403.20326.regime: The results apply asymptotically in the standard word RAM model for sparse inputs and restricted universe sizes.
2403.20326.hypothesized_generalization: The authors hint at generalizing the sparse general convolution algorithm to remove the restriction on the input vector length.

2404.00768.problem: The paper studies the robustness of posterior inference on the root vertex of a tree-structured broadcast process when a fraction of the leaf observations are adversarially corrupted.
2404.00768.methods: The authors analyze the performance of the canonical belief propagation algorithm under semi-random and spread adversarial corruption models.
2404.00768.regime: The results apply in the limit of infinite tree depth where the signal-to-noise ratio exceeds the Kesten-Stigum threshold.

2410.04771.problem: The paper addresses the complexity of computing the deterministic co-lexicographic width of a regular language from a given DFA.
2410.04771.methods: The authors use new algorithmic techniques to establish an upper bound and prove a matching conditional lower bound based on the Strong Exponential Time Hypothesis.
2410.04771.regime: The result applies asymptotically in terms of the DFA size $m$ and the width parameter $p \ge 2$ for minimum DFAs.

2412.11914.problem: The paper improves the upper bounds and determines the exact maximum number of unit distances for small point sets.
2412.11914.methods: The authors use combinatorial filtering with minimal forbidden subgraphs, totally unfaithful graph elimination, and a custom geometric embeddability solver.
2412.11914.regime: Small finite point sets of size n up to 21.

2501.00171.problem: The paper investigates the probability distribution of the minimal denominator degree and the distribution of the unique monic minimal denominator polynomial in function fields.
2501.00171.methods: The authors translate the minimal denominator problem into linear algebra using ranks of Hankel matrices and apply counting techniques over finite fields.
2501.00171.regime: The results apply to function fields over a finite field of constant characteristic with a finite residue field.
2501.00171.hypothesized_generalization: The authors hint at the minimal denominator problem in the infinite residue case, such as over the field of rational functions with real or complex coefficients, but note that their counting techniques do not apply.

2501.10203.problem: The paper aims to improve the bounds for sets lacking k-configurations and apply these results to the Erdős--Moser sum-free set problem.
2501.10203.methods: The authors combine the techniques of Kelley and Meka with those of Filmus, Hatami, Hosseini, and Kelman to establish new density bounds.
2501.10203.regime: Asymptotic in the size of the abelian group and the parameter k.
2501.10203.hypothesized_generalization: The authors hint at the optimality of their bounds up to the respective exponents of 1/12 and 1/2 in the parameters k and delta.

2503.09440.problem: The paper aims to reconstruct, simplify, and provide an electronic record of Farber's lost proof characterizing strongly chordal graphs as intersection graphs of compatible subtrees of a rooted weighted tree, while also providing an efficient algorithm to find a strong elimination order from this representation.
2503.09440.methods: The paper uses graph theory, tree-representation of chordal graphs, and a new algorithm that directly extracts a strong elimination order from a compatible tree-representation.
2503.09440.regime: Finite, simple, undirected graphs, specifically subclasses of chordal graphs.

2503.09591.problem: The paper investigates the existence of an edge-isoperimetric ordering on a specific two-dimensional Cayley graph of a lattice where vertices are connected if their distance is 1 or sqrt(3).
2503.09591.methods: The authors utilize computer-assisted proofs, specifically Python scripts for base cases, inductive steps, and sequence solutions, to establish the ordering.
2503.09591.regime: The result applies to a specific two-dimensional infinite lattice graph.

2503.16404.problem: The paper investigates the relationship between series-parallel graphs and their degeneracy within the hypercube.
2503.16404.methods: The authors employ structural graph theory, series-parallel decompositions, and hypercube embedding techniques.
2503.16404.regime: The results apply to finite series-parallel graphs and their embeddings into hypercubes of arbitrary dimension.

2503.17294.problem: The paper investigates the structural theory, realizability complexity, and algorithmic hardness of cycle patterns in directed graphs, particularly their application to solving mean payoff games.
2503.17294.methods: The authors use cycle patterns, arithmetic and Boolean circuits, linear decision trees, and polyhedral geometry to analyze game complexity and realizability.
2503.17294.regime: The results apply to finite directed graphs and games with arbitrary integer weight functions, focusing on the transition between polynomial and exponential weight scales.
2503.17294.hypod_generalization: The authors hint at generalizing their realizability insights to understand the size of integer points in more general polyhedral fans within geometric combinatorics.

2505.02685.problem: The paper aims to bound the mixing time and spectral gap of the censored random walk on monotone subsets of the hypercube.
2505.02685.methods: The authors analyze the spectral expansion of the induced subgraph using a robust version of the Poincaré inequality and directed Laplacian heat flow.
2505.02685.regime: The result applies to monotone subsets of the hypercube with constant density as the dimension n grows.
2505.02685.hypothesized_generalization: The authors hint at improving the mixing time bound of the censored random walk on monotone sets of constant density to O(n log n).

2505.03211.problem: The paper studies the noise sensitivity and variance lower bounds of the minimal left-right crossing passage times in first-passage percolation on a square.
2505.03211.methods: The authors establish a small ball probability estimate in the tail by perturbing the weights for tail events using a Mermin-Wagner type estimate.
2505.03211.regime: Asymptotic in the size of the square n.
2505.03211.hypothesized_generalization: The authors suggest that their variance lower bounds can be generalized to absolutely continuous weight distributions and that certain geometric assumptions on the limit shape are expected to hold for almost any distribution.

2506.07170.problem: The paper investigates the conditions under which a graph can be represented as a rectangular dual on cylindrical and toroidal surfaces.
2506.07170.methods: The authors extend planar rectangular dualization techniques and topological graph theory to characterize dual layouts on non-planar surfaces.
2506.07170.regime: Finite graphs embedded on cylinders and tori.

2507.15679.problem: The paper investigates Erdős's unit distance problem by finding rigid sub-frameworks within dense, highly non-generic point configurations in the plane.
2507.15679.methods: The authors combine graph rigidity theory, framework rigidity definitions, and combinatorial geometry incidence bounds.
2507.15679.regime: Asymptotic in the number of points n, focusing on configurations that maximize the number of unit distances.

2604.04188.problem: The paper addresses the noisy k-XOR distinguishing problem, showing that near-optimal graph expansion does not inherently imply computational hardness.
2604.04188.methods: The authors combine the expander graphs of Guruswami, Umans, and Vadhan with decoding algorithms for Reed-Muller codes from random errors.
2604.04188.regime: The result applies to the regime where k is polylogarithmic in the number of variables and the graph has near-optimal expansion.
2604.04188.hypothesized_generalization: Under standard conjectures on Reed-Muller codes over the binary erasure channel, the result generalizes to families with near-optimal expansion and polynomial-time algorithms at noise rates up to 1/2.

2604.08691.problem: The paper addresses the detection and recovery of a planted clique in a uniform hypergraph when only its projected adjacency matrix is observed.
2604.08691.methods: The authors analyze a spectral norm test for detection and a polynomial-time spectral method based on the leading eigenvector using a leave-one-out framework for recovery.
2604.08691.regime: The results apply asymptotically as the number of vertices $n$ grows, covering both dense and sparse background hyperedge probability regimes.
2604.08691.hypothesized_generalization: The authors hint at extending the recovery of hyperedges from graph projections to more general heterogeneous random hypergraph models with multiple edge degrees.

2604.18283.problem: The paper addresses whether upper and lower quantum functionals coincide for higher-order tensors and how to construct new spectral points in Strassen's asymptotic spectrum.
2604.18283.methods: The authors analyze laminar weightings, embedded three-tensors, and W-like states to construct new spectral points where upper and lower quantum functionals coincide.
2604.18283.regime: Asymptotic regime for higher-order tensors under Kronecker powers.
2604.18283.hypothesized_generalization: The authors hint at extending the equivalence of upper and lower quantum functionals to more general classes of weightings beyond laminar weightings.

2604.21531.problem: The paper determines the optimal kernelization bounds for constrained coloring problems, specifically finding the infimum kernel size for rainbow-free coloring of hypergraphs.
2604.21531.methods: The authors utilize an algebraic approach based on low-degree polynomials and universal algebra to establish both upper and lower kernelization bounds.
2604.21531.regime: The results apply to constraint satisfaction and coloring problems parameterized by the number of variables or the vertex-deletion distance to a disjoint union of cliques.
2604.21531.hypotheses_generalization: The authors hint at extending the characterization of kernel complexity to general non-Boolean constraint satisfaction problems over finite domains of size larger than two.

2604.22052.problem: The paper addresses whether space-efficient turnstile streaming algorithms can be simulated by linear sketches when the stream length is polynomial in the dimension.
2604.22052.methods: The authors use a Fourier-analytic framework and tools from additive combinatorics to extract discrete linear measurements from the streaming algorithm.
2604.22052.regime: Polynomial-length turnstile streams and non-uniform Read-Once Branching Programs (ROBPs).
2604.22052.hyphesized_generalization: The authors hint that their results extend to strict turnstile streams and non-uniform Read-Once Branching Programs (ROBPs).

2605.20579.problem: The paper establishes an explicit lower bound for the unit distance problem in the plane.
2605.20579.methods: The proof uses lattices from Golod-Shafarevich class field towers of number fields, relative class numbers, and projection techniques.
2605.20579.regime: Asymptotic in the number of points n.
2605.20579.hypothesized_generalization: The authors suggest potential improvements to the exponent using analytic and algebraic number theory techniques, and raise questions about the density of the point sets and the limits of the achievable exponents.
